log.why: Ticket 1 has less time left and testing dnaK directly evaluates the 0.395 leading hypothesis with high information gain.
Ticket 1 already has E0 growing, so testing 10 uM on Ticket 2 splits its posterior near the median.
E3 at 3 uM bisects Ticket 2 posterior (0.572 vs 0.428) and starts incubation immediately.
Ticket 3 has high uncertainty (top katG 0.263); E9 splits posterior mass nearly evenly (0.502 vs 0.498) while Ticket 2 incubates.
Ticket 2 is urgent with 0.483 peak posterior; 1 uM best splits the 0.441 vs 0.559 mass while starting incubation now.
dnaK holds a 0.880 posterior after E0; publishing now secures strong time and plate bonuses without risking diminishing returns.
Running E0 tests top candidate gyrA (0.432 posterior) while incubators are idle, either confirming it or shifting mass to metJ and fliC.
E5 splits Ticket 4's posterior nearly evenly (0.476 vs 0.523) and incubates while we publish Ticket 2 next.
Testing sodA on Ticket 4 splits its near-even posterior with lacZ while starting incubation before publishing expiring Ticket 2.
Ticket 2 expires in 10 s with 0.793 posterior for 3 uM; publishing now captures strong expected value before deadline.
Ticket 3 expires in 9s and gyrA has strong 0.895 posterior after E9 and E0 both lost the phenotype.
Run E2 on Ticket 5 to split its posterior near 50/50 while preparing to publish Ticket 4 during incubation.
Publishing Ticket 4 on lacZ (0.744 posterior) captures high expected value before its 22 s deadline and saves bench time.
Ticket 5 already leads at 3 µM (0.389); E3 splits the posterior nearly evenly (0.450 vs 0.550) to test it.
With E3 growing on Ticket 5, running E4 in parallel separates the 0.307 posterior at 10 µM from higher doses before round end.
Only 7s remain in the round, so new experiments cannot finish; publishing Ticket 5 at 0.535 posterior yields high positive expected value.
With 1 s left in the round and top posterior only 0.205, neither running nor publishing is profitable.
